project.cwe_name: Improper Control of Generation of Code ('Code Injection')

ground_truth.cwe_name: Improper Control of Generation of Code ('Code Injection')

parsed_output.evidence:
Root cause / sink: org.ff4j.core.MappingUtil#instanceFlippingStrategy (ff4j-core/src/main/java/org/ff4j/utils/MappingUtil.java:181-190), specifically line 183 `Class.forName(className)`/`classLoader.loadClass(className)` immediately followed by line 184 `clazz.newInstance()` — the cast to `Class<FlippingStrategy>` at line 183 is an unchecked generic cast that provides NO runtime type safety; the JVM does not verify assignability until a FlippingStrategy method is actually invoked, by which point the attacker's constructor has already run. Trust boundary: `className` originates from untrusted config/API input (properties file values, XML attribute `class`, JSON `flip.class`, or the raw HTTP request parameter `strategy` in the web console) and reaches this sink without any allow-list or isAssignableFrom check. Verified live: unpatched run prints "VULNERABLE" and exits 0; after inserting `if (!FlippingStrategy.class.isAssignableFrom(rawClazz)) throw ...` before newInstance(), the same command prints "NOT VULNERABLE" and exits 1 (then reverted, confirmed identical to HEAD via git diff).

Every distinct sink/source-to-sink path in the alert that a complete fix must guard:
1. ff4j-core/src/main/java/org/ff4j/utils/MappingUtil.java:181-190 `instanceFlippingStrategy` — Class.forName(className).newInstance() cast to FlippingStrategy. Reached from: PropertiesParser (properties `flip.strategy`/`flip.class` value, trace 2), FeatureJsonParser (JSON `flip.class`/classType field, traces in vuln #6, via MappingUtil.java:181-183 directly), and any other config-driven flip-strategy loader.
2. ff4j-core/src/main/java/org/ff4j/conf/XmlParser.java:432-443 `parseFlipStrategy` — a SEPARATE, duplicated sink: `Class.forName(clazzName).newInstance()` cast to FlippingStrategy, driven by the XML `<flipstrategy class="...">` attribute. Does not go through MappingUtil at all, so fixing MappingUtil alone will NOT close this path.
3. ff4j-web/src/main/java/org/ff4j/web/embedded/ConsoleOperations.java:104-108 `createFeature` — a THIRD independent sink: `Class.forName(strategy).newInstance()` cast to FlippingStrategy, driven directly by the raw, unauthenticated-adjacent HTTP request parameter `strategy` from the embedded admin console (`req.getParameter(STRATEGY)`). This is the most directly attacker-reachable variant (network input, no parsing indirection).
4. ff4j-core/src/main/java/org/ff4j/property/util/PropertyFactory.java:158-181 `createProperty(pName, pType, pValue, desc, fixedValues)` — sink is `Class.forName(pType).getConstructor(String.class, String.class).newInstance(pName, pValue)` at line 163-164, cast to `Property<?>`. `pType` reaches here from: PropertiesParser property `type=` values (via MappingUtil.mapPropertyType, trace 1), XmlParser property `type=` attribute (XmlParser.java:379-391, its own inline Class.forName+getConstructor call — a FOURTH, still separate duplication of the same pattern), PropertyJsonBean/MongoPropertyMapper (trace 5, path 1), FeatureJsonParser embedded custom-property JSON (trace 5, paths 2-3), and PropertyJsonParser (trace 5, path 4). All funnel into PropertyFactory.createProperty as the common downstream sink, but XmlParser.java:387 is an independent duplicate that must also be fixed even if PropertyFactory is hardened.
5. ff4j-core/src/main/java/org/ff4j/utils/MappingUtil.java:93-98 `mapPropertyType` is NOT itself a sink (pure string substitution / passthrough for unrecognized values) but is the shared "trust laundering" hop that lets a raw attacker string flow unchanged into sinks #4 whenever it doesn't match a known short alias — a fix here (e.g. rejecting unknown types outright) is one valid mitigation layer but does not substitute for validating at the actual construction sinks.
6. ff4j-core/src/main/java/org/ff4j/utils/MappingUtil.java:180-183 `className` param used by trace in vuln #6 (FeatureJsonParser flip `classType`) reaches the same MappingUtil sink as #1 — confirms MappingUtil.instanceFlippingStrategy is the converging sink for both properties- and JSON-sourced flip-strategy class names, but XmlParser (#2) and ConsoleOperations (#3) remain independent code paths.
parsed_output.expected_vulnerable_behavior: MappingUtil.instanceFlippingStrategy("pov-uid", "org.ff4j.pov.MappingUtilInjectionPoV$NotAFlippingStrategy", initParams) reflectively resolves and instantiates the attacker-named class via Class.forName(className).newInstance() BEFORE ever checking it is assignable to FlippingStrategy. The class's constructor runs (flips a static AtomicBoolean) even though it does not implement FlippingStrategy at all; only afterward does the implicit cast fail and get swallowed into a FeatureAccessException. The PoV observes the side-effect flag and prints "VULNERABLE" + exits 0. After a fix adds an isAssignableFrom (or allow-list) check prior to newInstance(), the attacker class is never constructed, the flag stays false, the PoV prints "NOT VULNERABLE" and exits 1.
parsed_output.notes: Targeted alert trace: vulnerability #2 (PropertiesParser flip-strategy trace, PropertiesParser.java:307→311 `flipStrategyClass`) and, by extension, its convergence point ff4j-core/utils/MappingUtil.java:181-190 `instanceFlippingStrategy`, which is also the terminal sink named directly in vulnerability #6's JSON traces (MappingUtil.java:181-183 `className`). I chose this sink over the PropertyFactory/PropertyType traces (vulnerabilities #1, #3, #5) because it is the simplest, most self-contained demonstration of the alert's stated root cause ("Expected base-type constraints must hold at every construction sink") — it requires only a no-arg constructor (no JDK gadget class or two-String-arg constructor hunting needed), it is 100% network/dependency-free to exercise (no XML/JSON parsing scaffolding, no servlet container), and it directly calls real, unmodified production code (org.ff4j.utils.MappingUtil, compiled from ff4j-core) rather than simulating the behavior. I validated the PoV both ways: it exits 0 (vulnerable) against the current HEAD, and exits 1 (blocked) after temporarily adding an `isAssignableFrom` guard at the sink, then reverted that temporary edit (confirmed via `git diff` against HEAD showing zero difference) so the worktree's tracked files are unmodified — only the new `.security-pipeline/pov/` directory is added. The `evidence` and `regression_hint` fields above enumerate the four other structurally-independent sinks (XmlParser's two separate Class.forName call sites, ConsoleOperations' HTTP-driven site, and PropertyFactory's (String,String)-constructor site) that a downstream patcher must also fix, since this PoV exercises only one of them.
parsed_output.regression_hint:
Invariant a correct fix must enforce, at EVERY one of the sinks listed above, before any constructor of the resolved class executes: the resolved `Class<?>` must be validated (via `isAssignableFrom` against the expected base type — `FlippingStrategy` for strategy sinks, `Property` for property-type sinks — or via an explicit allow-list of known implementation class names) BEFORE calling `newInstance()` / `Constructor.newInstance()`. Doing the check only via a post-construction cast (as today) is insufficient because the attacker's no-arg or (String,String) constructor has already run by the time the ClassCastException surfaces — any side effects (file writes, network calls, JNDI lookups, static initializers) already fired.

Known bypass variants the fix must also block, since each is a structurally-independent call site and patching only one leaves the others exploitable:
- MappingUtil.instanceFlippingStrategy (ff4j-core/utils/MappingUtil.java:183-184) — properties- and JSON-sourced flip-strategy class names.
- XmlParser.parseFlipStrategy (ff4j-core/conf/XmlParser.java:443) — XML `<flipstrategy class="...">` attribute, duplicate Class.forName+newInstance logic, not routed through MappingUtil.
- ConsoleOperations.createFeature (ff4j-web/web/embedded/ConsoleOperations.java:107-108) — raw HTTP request parameter `strategy`/`strategyParams`, the most directly network-reachable variant.
- PropertyFactory.createProperty (ff4j-core/property/util/PropertyFactory.java:163-164) — reflective (String,String)-constructor instantiation keyed by `pType`, reachable from properties, XML, JSON (FeatureJsonParser, PropertyJsonParser), and Mongo-mapped PropertyJsonBean inputs.
- XmlParser property `type=` attribute handling (ff4j-core/conf/XmlParser.java:379-391) — a second, independent inline duplicate of the PropertyFactory reflective-construction pattern; fixing PropertyFactory alone does not cover this because XmlParser calls `Class.forName(optionalType).getConstructor(...).newInstance(...)` itself rather than delegating to PropertyFactory.

Also verify the fix doesn't rely solely on string-based checks that are easy to bypass (e.g. checking `className.startsWith("org.ff4j.")` can be defeated by any third-party or classpath-local class under that prefix, or by classes registered via a custom ClassLoader set through `MappingUtil.setClassLoader`); prefer `isAssignableFrom` reflective checks plus, ideally, an explicit allow-list of concrete strategy/property classes shipped or explicitly registered by the application, applied uniformly across all five sinks above.
parsed_output.summary: Created a standalone Java PoV that drives the real production sink org.ff4j.utils.MappingUtil#instanceFlippingStrategy with an attacker-controlled class name that does not implement FlippingStrategy. The class's no-arg constructor executes as an observable side effect before the post-construction cast fails, proving the sink performs Class.forName(...).newInstance() with no base-type check. This is the shared root-cause pattern (unchecked reflective construction from an attacker string) that recurs across every trace in the alert: PropertiesParser flip-strategy/property-type parsing, XmlParser property-type and flip-strategy parsing, PropertyFactory.createProperty, FeatureJsonParser/PropertyJsonParser via MappingUtil, and the embedded web console's ConsoleOperations.createFeature.

parsed_output.patch_notes:
Root cause: multiple call sites did Class.forName(attackerString).newInstance() (or Constructor(String,String).newInstance()) and only checked the expected base type via an implicit cast AFTER construction, so the attacker's constructor (and any side effects: file writes, network calls, JNDI, static initializers) had already executed by the time the ClassCastException surfaced and was swallowed.

Fix: added MappingUtil.loadClass(String className, Class<T> expectedType) which does Class.forName/classLoader.loadClass, then checks expectedType.isAssignableFrom(rawClazz) and throws IllegalArgumentException immediately if not assignable — no instance is ever created for a class outside the expected type. This is now the single choke point used at every flip-strategy sink (MappingUtil.instanceFlippingStrategy, XmlParser.parseFlipStrategy, PropertiesParser.parseFeatures, YamlParser.parseFlipStrategy, ConsoleOperations.createFeature/updateFlippingStrategy) with expectedType=FlippingStrategy.class, and inside PropertyFactory.createProperty(String,String,String,String,Set) with expectedType=Property.class for property-type construction (which XmlParser, PropertiesParser and YamlParser's property-type parsing now delegate to instead of duplicating their own Class.forName+getConstructor logic).

Out of scope / intentionally not touched: ConsoleServlet.init / FF4jServlet.init load an FF4jProvider class from a servlet init-param (deployment-time trust boundary, configured by the application owner via web.xml, not runtime attacker input) — different threat model from the alert's traces. PropertyClass.fromString does Class.forName(v) but never calls newInstance() — it stores the resolved Class object itself as the property's value by design, not a construction sink, so it is not CWE-094.

Removed now-unreachable `catch (ClassNotFoundException e)` clauses in ConsoleOperations where Class.forName was replaced by MappingUtil.loadClass (which throws unchecked IllegalArgumentException instead), and dropped now-unused `java.lang.reflect.Constructor` imports from XmlParser, PropertiesParser and YamlParser after delegating to PropertyFactory.
parsed_output.risk_notes: Behavior change: constructing a flip-strategy or property with a class name that resolves but does not implement/extend the expected base type now fails fast with IllegalArgumentException/FeatureAccessException instead of the previous (also-failing, but post-construction) ClassCastException path — net effect is identical for legitimate configs (which always name a proper FlippingStrategy/Property subclass) and only changes behavior for malicious/malformed input, which is the intended fix. Ran full ff4j-core (1125 tests), ff4j-config-properties, ff4j-config-yaml, ff4j-web, and ff4j-utils-json test suites in the project Docker image — all green, 0 failures/errors. Re-ran the provided POV after the patch: it now prints 'NOT VULNERABLE' and exits 1 (previously exited 0/'VULNERABLE'). Two new regression tests added (MappingUtilsTest.testInstanceFlippingStrategyRejectsForeignClassBeforeConstruction, MappingUtilsTest.testLoadClassRejectsClassNotAssignableToExpectedType, PropertyFactoryTest.testCreatePropertyRejectsForeignClassBeforeConstruction) directly assert, via a static side-effect flag, that the attacker-named class's constructor never runs — mirroring the POV's own verification technique in the project's normal JUnit suite.
parsed_output.summary: Fixed CWE-094 unchecked reflective construction (Class.forName(...).newInstance()/Constructor.newInstance()) at every source-to-sink path named in the alert: flip-strategy loading (MappingUtil, XmlParser, PropertiesParser, YamlParser, ConsoleOperations) and property-type loading (PropertyFactory, XmlParser, PropertiesParser, YamlParser), plus the JSON parsers and Mongo mapper which already funneled through PropertyFactory/MappingUtil. Added a shared MappingUtil.loadClass(className, expectedType) helper that resolves the class and enforces expectedType.isAssignableFrom(rawClazz) BEFORE any constructor runs, throwing IllegalArgumentException otherwise. All flip-strategy sinks now call MappingUtil.loadClass(name, FlippingStrategy.class); PropertyFactory.createProperty now calls MappingUtil.loadClass(pType, Property.class) before getConstructor/newInstance. The duplicate inline Class.forName(...).getConstructor(...).newInstance(...) logic in XmlParser, PropertiesParser and YamlParser for property types was removed and replaced with a delegate to the now-hardened PropertyFactory.createProperty, eliminating the duplicated unguarded sinks rather than patching each copy separately.

parsed_output.diff_review: Reviewed patch_only.diff in full. All 8 changed files are directly relevant to the CWE-094 fix: MappingUtil.java (new loadClass helper + refactored instanceFlippingStrategy), PropertyFactory.java (createProperty now calls MappingUtil.loadClass(pType, Property.class) before getConstructor/newInstance), XmlParser.java, PropertiesParser.java, YamlParser.java (flip-strategy sinks now call MappingUtil.loadClass(...,FlippingStrategy.class).newInstance(); property-type sinks delegate to PropertyFactory.createProperty instead of duplicating unguarded Class.forName+getConstructor logic), ConsoleOperations.java (both HTTP-driven strategy sinks in createFeature and updateFlippingStrategy now use MappingUtil.loadClass), and two test files adding regression coverage (MappingUtilsTest, PropertyFactoryTest) that assert the attacker class's constructor never fires before the base-type check rejects it. No unrelated files touched, no broad/unrelated behavior changes, no weakening of the POV or vulnerable functionality removed without justification — the fix is a minimal, uniformly-applied base-type check inserted before every reflective construction call site named in the alert's traces. The .security-pipeline/pov/ directory is untouched by the patch (only new PoV artifacts, not modified).
parsed_output.pov_result: Independently reproduced both states by stashing/unstashing the patch in the worktree and rerunning `bash .security-pipeline/pov/run_pov.sh` via the docker wrapper: pre-patch (git stash) → stdout "VULNERABLE: MappingUtil.instanceFlippingStrategy reflectively constructed attacker-controlled class ... even though it does not implement FlippingStrategy", exit code 0. Post-patch (git stash pop, restored) → stdout "NOT VULNERABLE: attacker-controlled class name was rejected before construction; no side effect was observed.", exit code 1. This matches the orchestrator's own pov_before_patch/pov_after_patch logs exactly.

parsed_output.summary: Patch adds a single choke-point MappingUtil.loadClass(className, expectedType) that resolves a class and enforces expectedType.isAssignableFrom(rawClazz) BEFORE any newInstance()/Constructor.newInstance() call, and wires it into every reflective-construction sink named in the alert: MappingUtil.instanceFlippingStrategy, XmlParser.parseFlipStrategy and property-type parsing, PropertiesParser flip-strategy/property-type parsing, YamlParser flip-strategy/property-type parsing, PropertyFactory.createProperty (String,String constructor sink used by JSON/Mongo paths too), and ConsoleOperations' two HTTP-driven strategy-instantiation sites. Duplicate inline Class.forName+getConstructor logic in XmlParser/PropertiesParser/YamlParser was removed in favor of delegating to the now-hardened PropertyFactory.createProperty, eliminating rather than just patching each duplicate. Two new JUnit regression tests assert (via a static side-effect flag) that a foreign class's constructor never runs before the base-type check throws.
